label: L2
instruction:
You are a research LEADER or EXECUTOR in a user-authorized cross-domain idea-generation test. Use ONLY the supplied input file. No memory, other project files, other runs, network, direct scientific execution or delegation. You may use exec to read the input and write your JSON reply, including JSON/Python AST syntax validation without executing scientific code. Complete writing once and then return a short completion notification. All scientific computation and searches are requested in JSON and run by the broker.

The goal is to propose a specific research IDEA beyond the supplied information. A complete or correct new mechanism is NOT required. Explanatory questions, measurement designs, interventions, operational decisions and methods are eligible. A generic 'fit a better model', factor list, caution-only audit or restatement of documented leakage is not an idea increment. Choose a domain-relevant question and make a testable addition. Plausible conjectures with an explicit failure test are legitimate; clearly distinguish evidence from assumptions.

The original role principles and method index are provided. Apply them proportionately to this idea task; do not require a fully solved scientific theory. At most three method cards requested by leader are supplied to executor. No target paper answer exists. Disclose recognition of this public dataset or a remembered prior study. Familiarity is not itself disqualifying, but do not call a known result new.

All dataset rows are available to actual broker computation as pandas DataFrame DF and TABLES['main']. You receive exact column names, raw metadata, a univariate profile and fixed sample rows. Row-level independence and unavailable measurements matter. Do not claim observational associations establish interventions, or treat interpolated outcome labels as independent clinical observations. A new-data test is allowed if it names the measurement, unit, comparison, decision rule and alternative, rather than merely 'collect more data'.

L1 LEADER: propose EXACTLY THREE distinct candidate records, select one, give executor one focused development/critique task with acceptance conditions, and select up to 3 method_ids. Freeze predictions before any tool return. You may describe a desired calculation/search but do not issue executable requests. No computation is required merely to call an idea a candidate.

R1 EXECUTOR: critique the selected candidate, improve it if justified, and issue at most ONE computation and ONE Crossref search. Use computation when it can check an actual premise, contrast or feasibility. A negative result is useful; do not force agreement. Provide complete scientific code using DF; print compact valid JSON (<40k chars), runtime <30 s. No I/O. Allowed imports json/math/statistics/itertools/functools/collections/datetime/numpy/pandas/scipy/sklearn. Broker does not repair science or invent parameters. Submit genuine outputs only after execution is returned; in this turn requests are pending.

L2 LEADER FINAL: inspect all actual tool returns, including failures and limited literature coverage. Keep, revise, withdraw or block the idea. A revised uncomputed hypothesis must be labeled proposal-only. Give a concrete final idea if warranted; do not replace it with cautions alone. No further requests on this last turn. Record exactly what was learned, what changed, and the next falsifiable test.

Return ONE JSON object, no fences, with:
- recognition: dataset/source recognition or uncertain
- summary
- candidates: L1 exactly 3 records, later changed records if any; stable ids I1/I2/I3. Each record has id,title,question,new_claim,input_delta,domain_value,known_basis_refs,assumptions,variables_and_units,testable_prediction,alternative,discriminating_test,feasible_with_current_data,required_new_data,failure_condition,nearest_prior_query.
- selected_id
- method_ids: at most 3 ids
- task: {deliverable,acceptance,proposed_computation,proposed_search}, as appropriate
- critique: executor's concrete objections and improvements, otherwise []
- requests: executor only, at most [{type:'compute',id,idea_id,purpose,model_spec,code},{type:'search',id,idea_id,missing_relation,query,change_if_found}]. All scientific choices belong to roles. Use only alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen IDs.
- final: null except L2. L2 {status:'retained'|'revised'|'withdrawn'|'blocked',final_idea:full candidate record or null,evidence_level:'proposal_only'|'computed_candidate'|'observational_support'|'negative_result',what_changed,what_is_known,what_is_new_hypothesis,falsifier,minimum_next_test,tool_evidence_refs,nearest_work_comparison,novelty_status,limitations}.

Novelty has two meanings: the idea adds to the input, and the idea is new in world literature. Provide the first explicitly; claim the second only with actual supporting comparison. The search may return titles only. Do not infer abstract results/formulas from a title. Existing dataset prediction baselines, late-label leakage, time dependence or within-person grouping already stated in documentation do not become novel merely by renaming them.
original_role_principles:
# Leader 系统提示词 v1

你是科学调查的研究负责人。你面对的是一个尚未解释的现象。你的任务是选择下一项能推进认识的行动，组织已有知识、推导、计算和测量，使候选解释逐步产生可检验的预测。所有研究生成使用 gpt-6-luna。

## 运行输入与职责

组织者会提供 CASE_BRIEF、OBSERVATIONS、SOURCE_CARDS、MODEL_CARDS、ACTION_HISTORY、CAPABILITIES、BUDGET、BACKGROUND_CUTOFF、METHOD_INDEX，以及你请求的少量 METHOD_CARDS。缺失字段先标为 unknown。CAPABILITIES 中未声明可用的工具不能假装执行；可以向组织者申请。

你可以给同一个研究 agent 分阶段安排检索、机制构建、推导、拟合和反例分析。这些是工作阶段，不要求每项工作各建一个 agent。负责人也可以完成简短的代数或整理任务。计算和测量完成与否，以组织者返回的实际记录为准。

## 每轮选择下一步

1. 用一句话说明当前需要解释或预测的量。保留其测量定义、单位、时间尺度和独立重复单位。
2. 查看现有模型的缺口：缺背景知识、缺变量、缺机制连接、方程未闭合、参数不可识别、缺计算、预测失败、还是测量本身有歧义。允许多个缺口，优先处理阻塞当前目标的一个。
3. 从 METHOD_INDEX 申请最多三个相关方法卡。卡片不足时可以提出新方法，给出适用条件。方法库不是封闭的答案空间。
4. 选择一个主行动及一个结果依赖的备用行动。说明它分别会排除什么、补齐什么。不要同时安排互不依赖的大量泛泛任务。
5. 给研究 agent 一个能交付的任务：输入证据编号、所用方法、明确产物、可用计算/测量、预算和验收条件。
6. 返回后核对实际产物；成功则推进，失败则记录失败类型并修改任务。同一任务在输入和做法都不变时失败两次，就换方法或指出需要补充的资源。

比较行动时，依次考虑：是否补齐关键依赖；不同结果能否区分存活模型；输入和工具是否可得；费用与剩余预算。没有模型概率和观测噪声时，用定性的“信息价值代理”，不要伪造贝叶斯信息增益数字。

## 组合推导的工作方式

看到知识 A 和知识 B 时，允许尝试把它们结合。组合必须交代以下接口：

- A 的输出是否真的是 B 的输入：对象、变量定义、单位、空间和时间尺度是否一致？
- 各自成立的前提是否同时满足？共用变量、质量、能量或同一作用是否被重复计算？
- 连接 A 与 B 需要新增什么假设或测量？逐项标注为已知规律、当前观测、新假设或待估参数。
- 组合后的最小模型是什么？它比单独 A、单独 B 多预测哪一个可测结果？什么结果会否定这个连接？

可以采用串联、并联竞争、交互项、反馈、延迟、隐藏状态、空间耦合或尺度约化。只选择现象和证据支持的连接方式，不能为了凑组合强行加入。

把因果链画成“可操纵条件 → 中间可测状态 → 可观测结果”。在每条边标出依据和缺失证据。先补最关键的一条缺边，再拓展模型。类比提供候选关系；只有检查目标系统的适用条件后，才能把它当作目标中的机制假设。

## 从解释走到计算

当研究 agent 说“可能由某机制引起”，要求下一项具体产物：变量表、测量映射、约束、完整方程、可识别参数组合、数值解、稳定性条件或区分预测，按当前阶段选择一项。

计算模型包含：状态变量及单位、输入、观测函数、方程、参数及范围、初值/边界条件、噪声假设、用于拟合的数据。若含未定义函数或参数，标为模型草案，安排定义、约化或申请数据；可以探索性模拟，但不得用任意参数下的示意曲线冒充拟合或真实实验。

先做单位、守恒/收支、极限和适用条件检查，再拟合。结构提案与参数拟合分开记录。参数不可识别时，报告可识别组合或预测范围，并选择能区分它们的测量。

保持至少两个在当前证据下仍合理、且在某个可达条件下有不同预测的候选（若证据只支持一个，说明保留的替代解释及排除依据）。模型不得仅因换名称就算新结构。修改失败模型时说明改变的是结构、参数、适用范围、观测模型还是数值实现。

## 实验、检索与认识更新

申请新证据前，提交各候选的不同预测、测量定义、允许的结果范围和修订规则。已有数据重算、隐藏实测数据回放、模拟、新实体实验分别记录。

背景检索遵守组织者给出的最早公开时间截止，所有查询经过检索代理。日期不清的来源先隔离。只使用日期合格的版本及合格引用；早论文的新版网页、后加讨论和后续引用可能泄露答案。目标论文及其派生解读不提供给负责人或研究 agent。

每条知识保留来源 ID、版本/日期、假设和适用范围。每条经验结论保留测量 ID、模型版本、拟合数据和适用条件。预测失败后保留原预测，指出具体哪个假设受到反驳；带噪声的单次失败不自动否定整个模型族。

认识更新用简短表格表达：“此前判断—新证据—改变了哪条关系/参数/范围—下一项能区分的行动”。这是一份可审查的研究记录，不要求输出冗长的私人思维过程。

## 每轮输出格式

```text
目标：
当前认识：用证据 ID 概括已支持和仍待区分的内容。
主要缺口：
选择的方法卡：ID + 选择理由。
主任务：
  给谁/由谁执行：
  输入与可见来源：
  具体操作与交付物：
  验收条件：
  预算上限：
  行动前的区分预测或预期产物：
若结果为 X / Y，下一步分别是：
本轮新增假设：
预算变化与停止条件：
```

## 最终交付

给出已解释的现象、可计算模型、已推导关系、实际计算结果、事前预测及测量对照、认识更新记录和仍缺的关键测量。允许结论是部分解释或多个模型仍无法区分。最终目标是得到受证据支持的解释及预测；组织者隐藏的论文答案不作为可见的优化目标。
task_goal_override: This run evaluates specific idea generation, not complete mechanism discovery. Apply original principles at this stage; final scientific truth is not the acceptance target.

case.workflow: A building-energy team wants a concrete research question or monitoring/operation idea about household energy use, beyond another aggregate consumption predictor.
case.unit: Ten-minute observations over about 4.5 months in one house. Outdoor weather is partly interpolated from a nearby airport; random features rv1/rv2 are documented negative-control variables. Occupancy/appliance-level switching is not directly measured.

official_documentation.name: Appliances Energy Prediction
official_documentation.abstract: Experimental data used to create regression models of appliances energy use in a low energy building.

intro_paper.title: Data driven prediction models of energy use of appliances in a low-energy house
intro_paper.authors: L. Candanedo, V. Feldheim, Dominique Deramaix

additional_info.summary:
The data set is at 10 min for about 4.5 months. The house temperature and humidity conditions were monitored with a ZigBee wireless sensor network. Each wireless node transmitted the temperature and humidity conditions around 3.3 min. Then, the wireless data was averaged for 10 minutes periods. The energy data was logged every 10 minutes with m-bus energy meters. Weather from the nearest airport weather station (Chievres Airport, Belgium) was downloaded from a public data set from Reliable Prognosis (rp5.ru), and merged together with the experimental data sets using the date and time column. Two random variables have been included in the data set for testing the regression models and to filter out non predictive attributes (parameters).

For more information about the house, data collection, R scripts and figures, please refer to the paper and to the following github repository:

https://github.com/LuisM78/Appliances-energy-prediction-data

# 方法索引：44张卡

leader每轮按当前缺口取1–3张完整卡；下列不是必须依次执行的清单。可以提出库外方法。

## A 观察与问题构造

| ID | 方法 | 何时调用 |
|---|---|---|
| M01 | 观测量与潜在状态分开 | 同一个图像或汇总指标可以由不同变化产生。 |
| M02 | 因果图与替代路径 | 条件A/B有差异，但处理同时改变多种因素。 |
| M03 | 把复合现象拆成可分别解释的子问题 | 一句话同时要求解释出现、持续、大小和运动等多个现象。 |
| M04 | 把现象整理成约束集 | 已有多项观察，但假说只解释其中一项。 |
## B 约束、降维与初步推导

| ID | 方法 | 何时调用 |
|---|---|---|
| M05 | 从守恒与收支写方程 | 解释只有作用名称，没有状态如何变化。 |
| M06 | 量纲分析与无量纲组合 | 变量很多，拟议方程单位混乱，或想比较不同尺度。 |
| M07 | 竞争时间尺度与长度尺度 | 稳态直觉解释不了滞后、持续或空间差异。 |
| M08 | 极限、边界和退化情形推导 | 新方程看似合理，但尚无简单一致性检查。 |
| M09 | 对称性、坐标与不变量 | 不同表述可能等价，或关联依赖坐标定义。 |
| M10 | 可分解性与标度折叠 | 高维函数难以推导，但可能由较低维关系组成。 |
## C 知识获取与跨领域迁移

| ID | 方法 | 何时调用 |
|---|---|---|
| M11 | 按缺失知识检索 | 不知道一个过程的成立条件、测量方法或本构关系。 |
| M12 | 按功能或关系寻找外领域知识 | 本领域搜索反复返回同样解释。 |
| M13 | 结构类比映射 | 找到了灵感，但不知道如何用于当前系统。 |
| M14 | 把论文知识提取为可连接模块 | 文献很多，却无法据此建立模型。 |
## D 机制组合与表示修订

| ID | 方法 | 何时调用 |
|---|---|---|
| M15 | 机制图补桥与串联组合 | 分别知道A影响B、C影响D，却解释不了从处理到结果的整条链。 |
| M16 | 并行过程的竞争与耦合收支 | 两个机制可能同时存在，而非非此即彼。 |
| M17 | 交互项与非加性机制 | 两个因素单独影响弱，合并后出现异常响应。 |
| M18 | 反馈与延迟组合 | 现象有振荡、过冲、适应或长时间滞后。 |
| M19 | 隐藏状态、记忆与路径依赖 | 相同当前输入对应不同结果，误差依赖历史。 |
| M20 | 从整体模型扩展到空间模型 | 整体平均解释不了不同位置的差异。 |
| M21 | 异质性、随机性与群体混合 | 均值变化可能来自个体动力学，也可能来自群体组成。 |
| M22 | 尺度约化与有效变量 | 组合模型过大，无法估计或计算。 |
## E 推导、计算与参数

| ID | 方法 | 何时调用 |
|---|---|---|
| M23 | 方程闭合与计算依赖检查 | 出现未定义g/h、成核规则、力或通量，无法实际计算。 |
| M24 | 稳态、局部稳定性与阈值推导 | 需要解释何时出现新状态、何时保持或消失。 |
| M25 | 前向计算与观测预测 | 解释已有公式但还没有可对照数据的数值预测。 |
| M26 | 符号回归与方程骨架搜索 | 变量已知，关系形式未知，且有足够数值样本。 |
| M27 | 稀疏动力学与空间方程识别 | 有足够时间或时空测量，且合理假设动力学在候选库中稀疏。 |
| M28 | 结构与参数分离拟合 | 研究者凭文字选参数，或把优化失败当成结构错误。 |
| M29 | 参数与机制的可识别性 | 不同参数/机制拟合相近，却得出不同解释。 |
| M30 | 敏感度与不确定性传播 | 已有模型，但不知道哪些参数决定结论。 |
## F 模型批评与区分实验

| ID | 方法 | 何时调用 |
|---|---|---|
| M31 | 残差结构与后验预测检查 | 总体误差可接受，但局部条件或分布特征不对。 |
| M32 | 针对反例做最小结构修改 | 已有一次明确失败，但新提案只是换词。 |
| M33 | 选择能区分候选的实验 | 多个模型都解释现有数据。 |
| M34 | 阻断、匹配与因子组合实验 | 几个原因随处理一起变化，或怀疑交互作用。 |
| M35 | 边界探测与外推条件 | 候选在已见范围相近，需要检验其适用域。 |
| M36 | 测量伪影与替代观测模型 | 结论依赖阈值、共享分母、坐标、轨迹长度或筛选规则。 |
## G 修订与证据管理

| ID | 方法 | 何时调用 |
|---|---|---|
| M37 | 把失败变成后续生成约束 | 模型承认失败，下一轮却原样再提。 |
| M38 | 证据强弱、反证与停止 | 证据越来越多，但混入重复信息或反复挑选检验。 |
| M39 | 模型等价、去重与结构差异 | 候选越来越多，但只是变量改名或重参数化。 |
| M40 | 旧证据回归与局部适用范围 | 修订解释了新反例，却破坏旧规律。 |
## H 研究调度与交付

| ID | 方法 | 何时调用 |
|---|---|---|
| M41 | 模型空间扩展 | 可靠观测超出现有所有候选，参数重拟合也不能解释。 |
| M42 | 从目标倒排推导依赖 | 知道最终想预测什么，但 agent 不断泛泛讨论。 |
| M43 | 按真实重复单位做独立预测 | 拟合很好，但数据切分可能把同一轨迹或批次分到两边。 |
| M44 | 最小交付与预算停止 | 工作不断扩展，始终没有可审查结果。 |

method_cards.group: D 机制组合与表示修订
method_cards.name: 隐藏状态、记忆与路径依赖
method_cards.trigger: 相同当前输入对应不同结果，误差依赖历史。
method_cards.required_inputs: 完整输入历史、重复轨迹、测量模型。
steps: 先查遗漏已测变量和时间对齐
加入一个有可测代理的潜在状态
构造相同当前输入、不同历史的两次实验
method_cards.deliverable: 状态含义、更新式和可区分历史效应。
method_cards.failure_or_limit: 新增潜变量易吸收任何误差；不能从单条轨迹识别其物理含义。
method_cards.if_blocked: 检查M29可识别性；无法区分则保留预测范围。

reply.recognition: Recognized from supplied metadata as UCI Appliances Energy Prediction (UCI 374), associated with Candanedo et al. (2017), Data driven prediction models of energy use of appliances in a low-energy house. No remembered result is presented as new.
reply.summary: Propose a testable monitoring idea for one-household energy use beyond another aggregate predictor. Evidence: 19,735 ten-minute observations from one house over about 4.5 months; aggregate Appliances and lights energy, room temperature/humidity sensors, north-side outdoor T6/RH_6, partly interpolated airport weather, and documented random features rv1/rv2. The proposed increment tests whether delayed zone-specific thermal response adds an operational signal to aggregate energy monitoring. It cannot identify occupancy, appliance switching, or causal effects.

candidates.title: Thermal after-response as a monitor for sustained high household appliance load
candidates.question: After a high Appliances energy interval, is there a delayed increase in laundry and ironing zone temperature beyond matched low-load periods with similar clock time, pre-event temperatures, and outdoor temperature change?
candidates.new_claim: Input-level increment: test a preregistered lagged thermal-response contrast as a monitoring signal for sustained high aggregate appliance-energy episodes, rather than predicting the same-interval aggregate target. This is a hypothesis about observability, not device or occupant attribution or a literature novelty claim.
candidates.input_delta: The task frames the data as regression and describes room sensors, ten-minute aggregation, and aggregate Appliances energy. The proposed addition links high-load episodes to a future 30-60 minute zone-temperature response and monitoring use. T3 is the laundry room and T7 the ironing room per supplied variable information.
candidates.domain_value: If prospectively validated, a delayed zone response could flag sustained energy episodes for review and prioritize where to add submeters. It cannot identify a device or justify automated control by itself.
known_basis_refs: materials.official_documentation.variables: Appliances and lights are separately measured energy in Wh; T3 is laundry-room temperature; T7 is ironing-room temperature.

materials.official_documentation.additional_info: energy is logged every ten minutes; wireless temperature/humidity readings are averaged over ten-minute periods; two random variables were included for regression testing.
materials.case.unit: one house, about 4.5 months; outdoor weather is partly interpolated; occupancy/appliance-level switching is not directly measured.
materials.data_profile: 19,735 rows; Appliances quantiles are supplied at 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 1.0 only (median 60 Wh, maximum 1,080 Wh); no 90th percentile is assumed.
assumptions: A portion of some sustained electrical loads may produce detectable room heat, but fraction and location are unknown.
High aggregate Appliances energy can include heterogeneous devices and cannot be equated with one appliance or activity.
Clock time, pre-event thermal state, and observed weather suffice for an initial observational contrast; residual confounding and interpolation error remain.
Rows are serially dependent; day-level or longer blocks, not individual rows, must govern uncertainty.

variables_and_units.exposure: Appliances, Wh per ten-minute interval; define high-load threshold before inspecting post-event temperatures and specify event merging.
variables_and_units.separate_load: lights, Wh per ten-minute interval; retain or match because it is separately measured.
variables_and_units.primary_outcome: Mean of T3 and T7 temperature change in degrees C from the pre-event 30-minute mean to the 30-60 minute post-event mean.
variables_and_units.covariates: T_out in degrees C (airport-derived, partly interpolated), T6 in degrees C (north-side outdoor sensor), pre-event T3/T7 in degrees C, clock time, and day of week.
variables_and_units.placebo: Same temperature contrast over the 30-60 minutes before the high-load event.
variables_and_units.independent_unit: One household time series; use contiguous day-level or longer blocks for uncertainty, not row-wise independence.

candidates.testable_prediction: Compared with low-load controls matched on clock time, pre-event T3/T7, and observed outdoor conditions, high-load events will have a positive mean 30-60 minute post-event T3/T7 temperature-change contrast, with a day-block confidence interval excluding zero. The corresponding pre-event lead contrast should be near zero. Freeze direction and window before computation.
candidates.alternative: The apparent response reflects weather or time-of-day structure, reverse timing, sensor averaging, interpolation, or selection of unusual periods; alternatively, heterogeneous load location and heat output leave no stable thermal signature.
candidates.discriminating_test: Run a matched event study with day-block uncertainty. Compare the predeclared post-event contrast with the pre-event lead placebo and matched low-load exposure. Report independent event days and sensitivity to high-load threshold. A prospective follow-up should log room-level plug/submeter Wh and device activity to test the monitoring interpretation.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: The broker has the complete timestamped dataframe and required energy and sensor columns, so observational lag and placebo contrasts are computable. Results establish only a single-house association, not device attribution, causal heating, or generalization.
candidates.required_new_data: For monitoring validation, collect synchronized room-level plug/submeter Wh, appliance on/off labels, and room temperature at ten-minute or finer resolution in multiple homes. Record occupancy only if activity attribution is intended. Compare high-load episodes with matched low-load periods and predeclare alert precision or sensitivity/specificity.
candidates.failure_condition: Withdraw the thermal-monitoring signal if the post-event contrast is non-positive or its day-block interval includes zero, if the pre-event lead is comparably positive, or if the signal is not robust to reasonable event-threshold and weather-matching choices.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query to test proximity: residential appliance energy event detection using indoor temperature sensors, lagged thermal response, and submeter ground truth. The supplied 2017 paper concerns data-driven prediction of appliance energy; its uninspected full text is not used to claim novelty.

candidates.title: Zone-specific thermal coupling as an operational ventilation-change monitor
candidates.question: Do zone-specific lags between north-side outdoor T6 and indoor temperatures T1-T9 reveal periods of increased indoor-outdoor thermal coupling that merit ventilation or envelope inspection?
candidates.new_claim: Input-level increment: evaluate a change-point monitor based on zone response lag to measured north-side outdoor temperature, then validate whether it corresponds to window/ventilation state. This proposal does not claim the data measure window opening or building heat loss.
candidates.input_delta: The data include indoor temperatures by named room, T6 measured outside on the north side, and airport T_out with some interpolation. The proposed target is a changing zone-specific response lag, not aggregate energy prediction.
candidates.domain_value: A validated flag could direct an energy team to inspect unusual ventilation or envelope conditions before interpreting consumption changes as occupant behavior.
known_basis_refs: materials.official_documentation.variables: T1-T9 are room-specific temperatures; T6 is outside on the north side; T_out is airport weather.
materials.official_documentation.additional_info: room temperature/humidity observations were averaged over ten-minute periods; hourly airport weather was interpolated.
materials.case.unit: single house with no direct occupancy or appliance-switching measurement.
assumptions: T6 and indoor sensors are sufficiently synchronized to estimate lag at ten-minute resolution.
Rapid zone response can arise from ventilation or envelope coupling, but solar gains, internal heat, sensor placement, and other causes are alternatives.
Enough independent outdoor-temperature transitions exist to assess feasibility; unknown until computation.

variables_and_units.input: T6 and T_out, degrees C at ten-minute intervals.
variables_and_units.response: T1-T9, degrees C at ten-minute intervals.
variables_and_units.diagnostic: Zone-specific lag or response coefficient with a defined estimation window and uncertainty.
variables_and_units.validation_target: Window/ventilation state and HVAC state, measured prospectively; neither is supplied.

candidates.testable_prediction: If useful, candidate periods with shorter T6-to-indoor response lag in one zone will be associated with independently logged window/ventilation changes there, compared with matched periods without such changes.
candidates.alternative: Lag shifts reflect seasonal drift, airport interpolation, indoor gains, sensor placement, or autocorrelation rather than ventilation or envelope state.
candidates.discriminating_test: Assess lag stability in blocked time segments using available sensors, then prospectively compare flagged and unflagged ten-minute windows against window contacts and HVAC logs, with sensitivity and false-alert rate fixed in advance.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Descriptive lag stability is testable; identifying ventilation events or diagnostic accuracy is impossible without state labels.
candidates.required_new_data: Window-contact and HVAC on/off logs, plus repeated measurements in several homes and zones, synchronized with T6, T_out, and T1-T9.
candidates.failure_condition: Reject the monitor if estimated lag shifts are not reproducible across blocked periods or do not predict logged state changes above a prespecified baseline alert rate.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query to test proximity: residential window opening detection from indoor-outdoor temperature time series and zone thermal response.

candidates.title: Persistent overnight appliance energy as a standby-load audit trigger
candidates.question: Does aggregate Appliances energy persist overnight when lights are zero and measured room temperatures are stable, enough to justify a plug-level standby-load audit?
candidates.new_claim: Input-level increment: turn recurring low-activity overnight consumption into a defined audit trigger, separating an operational screening rule from an unsupported claim that the energy is standby consumption.
candidates.input_delta: The task identifies separately measured Appliances and lights energy at ten-minute cadence. The proposed use detects recurring overnight energy persistence and triggers submeters rather than fitting another aggregate predictor.
candidates.domain_value: A screening rule could prioritize homes or periods for plug-level auditing and potential standby-load reduction.
known_basis_refs: materials.official_documentation.variables: Appliances and lights are separate energy variables in Wh.
materials.official_documentation.additional_info: energy is logged at ten-minute intervals.
materials.data_profile: Appliances has supplied median 60 Wh; overnight-specific summaries are not supplied.
assumptions: Clock time defines an overnight window, but lights=0 and stable temperatures do not prove occupant absence or lack of active devices.
A persistent aggregate floor could include refrigeration, heating, or necessary loads and cannot be called standby without device measurements.

variables_and_units.energy: Appliances and lights, Wh per ten-minute interval.
variables_and_units.context: Timestamp and T1-T9, degrees C, used for a prespecified stable-temperature condition.
variables_and_units.audit_unit: Contiguous overnight episode and household, not independent ten-minute rows.

candidates.testable_prediction: A subset of overnight blocks with lights=0 and stable room temperatures will show recurring Appliances energy above the low-load floor on multiple nights; plug-level follow-up should identify a measurable, controllable portion.
candidates.alternative: Energy is necessary refrigeration/heating or unmeasured occupant/device use; the screening condition may not predict controllable standby energy.
candidates.discriminating_test: Estimate recurrence of the defined overnight condition in the current series, then instrument circuits with plug-level submeters for at least two weeks. Compare flagged and matched unflagged nights and quantify controllable Wh/day.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Recurrence of aggregate overnight patterns is computable, but occupancy absence and standby-device attribution are unobserved.
candidates.required_new_data: Plug-level Wh by device or circuit, occupancy/activity diary or sensor if making absence claims, and repeated nights across households.
candidates.failure_condition: Do not use the screen for standby-load interventions if flagged periods lack a reproducible controllable plug-level load above matched unflagged baseline.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query to test proximity: residential standby energy detection from smart meter load profiles, night baseload screening, and plug-level validation.

Do not report row-wise p-values as independent evidence or infer causal/device-specific effects. Return complete executable analysis code only if requesting computation; it must use DF, avoid I/O, print compact valid JSON, and run within broker limits.

Freeze high-load event thresholding and episode merging before inspecting outcomes; compare T3/T7 mean temperature change from the pre-event 30-minute baseline to the 30-60 minute post-event window against controls matched on clock time, pre-event temperatures, and T_out/T6. Report contrast in degrees C, day-block uncertainty, event/event-day counts, identically defined pre-event lead placebo, and sensitivity to threshold and matching. No results exist in this L1 turn.

task.deliverable: Critique I1 and specify one reproducible computation and one targeted Crossref search. Preserve the frozen directional prediction; treat output as single-house observational evidence only.
acceptance: Use >100 Wh for two consecutive ten-minute intervals as the main event rule, merge runs separated by one non-high interval, and report a >150 Wh threshold sensitivity.
Use complete contiguous windows, same-weekday controls within 60 minutes of clock time, calipers of 1 C on pre-event mean T3/T7 and 2 C on T6 and T_out, and nearest matching without replacement.
Report paired changes for the post window and identically defined lead placebo, with event counts and a 1,000-resample event-day bootstrap interval; do not treat rows as independent.
State that matched observational contrasts cannot establish intervention effects, appliance identity, occupancy, or generalization across homes.
Report search evidence only to the level of returned Crossref metadata; a title alone cannot establish study findings or novelty.
task.proposed_computation: One matched event study on complete DF, using the exact specification in compute request C1. No computation has run in this executor turn.
task.proposed_search: One Crossref query for residential appliance-energy event monitoring from lagged indoor room-temperature response, with submeter or appliance-state validation.

critique: The selected idea adds a useful lagged monitoring question, but L1 left “high-load,” episode merging, matching tolerances, edge handling, and the placebo contrast underspecified. Without those choices, event counts and the primary estimate could depend on analyst decisions after seeing outcomes.

T3 and T7 identify room locations, not the appliances contributing energy; the proposed contrast is a sensor association, not evidence of heat from a specific load or a causal effect. Single-house event days, not 19,735 rows, are the uncertainty units.

I made the prediction operational before requesting computation: >100 Wh in two consecutive intervals, prespecified merge rule, fixed 30-minute windows and lead placebo, explicit matching calipers, day-block bootstrap, and a >150 Wh sensitivity. If controls or independent event days are too few, the requested result should report infeasibility rather than relax definitions after inspection.

requests.purpose: Check whether the preregistered matched lagged thermal contrast and lead placebo are estimable and directionally consistent in the supplied single-house series; return counts and day-level uncertainty, not a causal estimate.
requests.model_spec: Main event: Appliances >100 Wh for at least two adjacent ten-minute rows; event time is run start; merge runs separated by one non-high row. Controls have Appliances <=100 Wh throughout +/-60 minutes. Match without replacement on same weekday, circular clock-time distance <=60 minutes, pre-event mean(T3,T7) difference <=1 C, and T6 and T_out differences <=2 C, selecting minimum standardized squared distance. Outcome is mean(T3,T7) at +30,+40,+50 minutes minus mean at -30,-20,-10 minutes; lead placebo is mean at -30,-20,-10 minus mean at -60,-50,-40. Require contiguous ten-minute rows and complete windows. Bootstrap paired contrasts after averaging within event day, 1000 resamples with seed 42. Repeat at >150 Wh as threshold sensitivity.

requests.missing_relation: Whether prior residential energy-monitoring work has tested delayed indoor room-temperature responses after aggregate appliance-load events, especially against submeter or appliance-state ground truth, and whether this exact monitoring relation is already established.
requests.query: ("appliance energy" OR "residential energy") AND ("indoor temperature" OR "room temperature") AND (event detection OR event monitoring OR submeter OR appliance state) AND (lag OR delayed response)

request.purpose: Check whether the preregistered matched lagged thermal contrast and lead placebo are estimable and directionally consistent in the supplied single-house series; return counts and day-level uncertainty, not a causal estimate.
request.model_spec: Main event: Appliances >100 Wh for at least two adjacent ten-minute rows; event time is run start; merge runs separated by one non-high row. Controls have Appliances <=100 Wh throughout +/-60 minutes. Match without replacement on same weekday, circular clock-time distance <=60 minutes, pre-event mean(T3,T7) difference <=1 C, and T6 and T_out differences <=2 C, selecting minimum standardized squared distance. Outcome is mean(T3,T7) at +30,+40,+50 minutes minus mean at -30,-20,-10 minutes; lead placebo is mean at -30,-20,-10 minus mean at -60,-50,-40. Require contiguous ten-minute rows and complete windows. Bootstrap paired contrasts after averaging within event day, 1000 resamples with seed 42. Repeat at >150 Wh as threshold sensitivity.

sources.title: Residential electricity current and appliance dataset for AC-event detection from Indian dwellings
sources.original_abstract:
Abstract 
                   Air Conditioners (ACs) have become a major contributor to residential electricity consumption in India. Non-intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) can be used to understand residential AC use and its contribution to electricity consumption. NILM techniques use ground truth information along with meter readings to train disaggregation algorithms. There are datasets available for disaggregation, but no dataset is available for a hot tropical country like India especially for AC event detection. Our dataset’s primary objective is to help train NILM algorithms for AC event detection and compressor operations. The dataset comprises of home-level electrical current consumption and manually tagged AC ground truth (ON/OFF status) data at 1-min interval, indoor environment temperature and relative humidity readings at 5-min interval and dwelling, AC and household characteristics. The data was collected from 11 homes located in a composite climate zone-Hyderabad, India for 19 summer days (May) 2019. The dataset consists of 1.6 million data points and 450 AC cycles with each cycle having a runtime of more than 60 min (> 2000 compressor ON/OF cycles). Public availability of such a dataset will allow researchers to develop, train and test NILM algorithms that recognize AC and identify compressor operations.
